findings.title: Update invalidation can miss login-cache invalidation because it uses an organization-aware original model
findings.body: In update(), the original model is fetched via getById(), which wraps the model so isEnabled() also checks whether the linked organization is enabled. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() then applies LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate(), which includes the enabled check. If the linked organization is disabled, the original model fails the predicate even though the IDP itself is storage-enabled. An update that makes the IDP unsuitable for login while the organization is disabled (for example setting hideOnLogin or linkOnly to true) can therefore have both original and updated predicates evaluate to false, so no login-cache invalidation is registered. When the organization is later enabled again, stale cached getForLogin results may still include an IDP that should be hidden or link-only. The original state should be evaluated with the raw storage model, or invalidation should be conservative here.

findings.title: getForLogin does not check invalidation of the requested organization
findings.body: getForLogin() only checks whether the realm/fetch-mode cache key is invalid. Unlike getByOrganization(), it does not check whether the supplied organizationId itself has been invalidated. If an organization is updated, disabled, removed, or its IDP association changes in a way that registers an organization invalidation, this method can still serve a stale cached list for that organization. Because the cached list is later resolved only by ID, the result may no longer match the requested organization or login availability.

findings.title: Cached getForLogin results are returned without revalidating login eligibility
findings.body: After a cache hit, getForLogin() resolves the cached internal IDs and returns them without re-applying LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() or verifying that each provider still matches the requested FetchMode and organizationId. Correctness therefore depends entirely on invalidations being perfect. Given the update-invalidation issue with organization-aware enabled state and the missing organization invalidation check, this can return providers that are currently disabled, hidden, link-only, or associated with a different organization. Filtering the resolved models before returning would make the cache robust against missed invalidations.

findings.title: Single per-realm login cache entry grows with every distinct organization search
findings.body: The login cache stores one IdentityProviderListQuery per realm and FetchMode, with internal search keys for each requested organizationId. Every distinct organization ID used in getForLogin is merged into the same cache object. In realms with many organizations, this single cache entry can become large, and each new organization search invalidates and rewrites the whole entry, causing cache churn and potential contention. A per-organization cache key or bounded structure would avoid unbounded growth and repeated invalidation of the shared entry.

findings.title: broker_public changes on realm-level IDPs may not invalidate ORG_ONLY login cache
findings.body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() skips invalidation when both old and new models satisfy the login predicate and the organization ID is unchanged. For an IDP with organizationId == null, the predicate is true regardless of the broker_public config. However the default getForLogin(ORG_ONLY, null) query filters by OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC, so changing broker_public on a realm-level IDP can change the ORG_ONLY result set. Because the organization ID remains null, this update can leave the ORG_ONLY login cache stale.

findings.title: Test cleanup removes literal alias 'alias' instead of the created identity provider alias
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup registration uses testRealm().identityProviders().get('alias')::remove instead of using the generated alias such as 'idp-alias-' + i. This does not remove the identity providers created by the test and may cause cleanup failures or state leakage into other tests. The same pattern appears again for the later created idp-alias-20 cleanup.
